verdictBasis: 0 blockers, 1 SHOULD-FIX, 0 advisories. ACCEPT was gated at 0 blockers AND 0 SHOULD-FIX.
verdictStatement: The V6-S1 repair is real and complete on the coverage question I raised. fixtureMemberMap grows from 50 keys to 72, adding all eleven AT-* acceptance-test halves and all eleven AT-ARCHIVE-* golden and negative cases, with nothing removed; I checked the obligation side independently and every AT class from AT-1 to AT-8 and every goldenAndNegativeCases member now resolves to a key. The two trusted-install halves are keyed with producer none, expected blocked-on-ride and explicit rides on ID-DEP-P3/DR-112 and ID-DEP-P3/DR-112/DR-110, which is exactly the parked standing they should carry, and all nine blocked-on-ride members carry a ride. fixtureClassCoverage now admits TC-*, AT-* and AT-ARCHIVE-* keys and states that the AT keys are required members. The items that had to stay repaired are intact by byte-identity: archiveProfile, acceptanceTests and fixtureGeneration are unchanged from v6, so the all-spaces checksum mask with its explicit 'A NUL in the mask is forbidden', the 100/101-byte capacity surfaced as typed non-success rather than hidden, and the ban on class-wide stand-ins all survive. What withholds acceptance is that the extension introduced a disjunctive expected outcome the map's own discipline forbids: eight of the eleven new archive members carry 'refuse:profile-or-admission', a token that appears nowhere in v6, is defined nowhere in v7, and sits against a discipline sentence that says each key has exactly one expected outcome.

shouldFix.title: Eight new archive members carry a disjunctive expected outcome, contradicting the map's own one-expected-outcome discipline

measurement.theDiscipline: fixtureMemberMap.discipline states: 'Each key has exactly one producer and one expected outcome. FG-1 is this map.' That sentence is the member-level keying CODEX-V4-S1 established and the dispatch lists class-level alternatives among the things that must stay repaired.
measurement.theViolation: I inventoried the expected value of all 72 members. Eight carry 'refuse:profile-or-admission': AT-ARCHIVE-BODY-MISMATCH, TARGET-MISMATCH, EXTRA-MEMBER, MISSING-MEMBER, NAME-101, LINK-101, TYPEFLAG-NUL and CHKSUM-SPACES. That is a disjunction of two refusal layers, so the discipline sentence is false as written for eight of seventy-two keys.
measurement.newlyIntroduced: I ran the same inventory over v6's fifty members: the token count for any disjunctive expected value is zero. Every v6 member carried a single outcome, several pinned to an exact subcode such as refuse:RJ-4/UNSIGNED or refuse:RJ-6/DUPLICATE_JSON_KEY. This pattern arrives with v7.
measurement.undefined: There is no expected-outcome vocabulary, enum, or defining sentence for 'refuse:profile-or-admission' anywhere in the artifact. All eight occurrences are the member entries themselves.
measurement.theLayerIsDeterminable: This is not a principled reservation the contract had to make. Its own text names the deciding check in every one of the eight cases: admissionChecks lists 'chksum recomputes with the all-spaces mask', 'no extra members', 'no missing members', 'no PAX/GNU typeflags' and the 'member/body/target/type/mode bijection', which covers six of them; and doesNotMintSchemaCaps names PATH-EXCEEDS-USTAR-NAME and LINKTARGET-EXCEEDS-USTAR-LINKNAME as 'profile-capacity refusals owned here', which covers NAME-101 and LINK-101.

shouldFix.whyThisIsTheRightSeverity: It is not a blocker and nothing fails open: both arms of the disjunction are refusals, so no adapter can pass one of these members by selecting an arm, and no authorization or packager choice creeps in. But a conformance report keyed by these members cannot distinguish a profile-layer refusal from an admission-layer one, which is precisely the discrimination member-level keying exists to provide, and the artifact asserts a property here that eight of its own members do not have. It is also this generation's own work, in the extension my V6-S1 asked to be made 'under the same one-producer / one-expected discipline'.
shouldFix.contrastingCaseIConsideredAndDidNotFault: AT-7 carries 'pass-or-blocked-on-ride', which is also a disjunction. I do not count it, because its arm-selection rule is stated — the AT-7 conformance duty says 'Missing owner gate => blocked-on-ride' — so which arm applies is decidable from the contract. The eight archive members have no such rule, which is the difference and also the shape of the fix.
shouldFix.minimumRepair: Give each of the eight the single outcome its own contract already determines: the six covered by admissionChecks become the admission refusal naming that check, and NAME-101 and LINK-101 become the profile-capacity refusals PATH-EXCEEDS-USTAR-NAME and LINKTARGET-EXCEEDS-USTAR-LINKNAME that doesNotMintSchemaCaps already owns. If any case genuinely must leave the layer open, define 'refuse:profile-or-admission' as a named outcome with a stated arm-selection rule the way AT-7 does, and amend the discipline sentence so it stops claiming exactly one outcome per key.

attacksAttemptedAndFailed: That the AT-* extension is nominal. The obligation side was enumerated independently and every AT class and archive case resolves to a key.
That adding AT keys quietly dropped TC keys. No key was removed; the 50 v6 members all survive.
That the declared counts are decorative. mapKeyCount, acceptanceTestKeyCount and archiveGoldenKeyCount all match what I counted.
That a blocked-on-ride member exists without a ride. All nine carry one.
That an earlier repair regressed while attention was on the map. archiveProfile, acceptanceTests and fixtureGeneration are byte-identical to v6.
That a member has alternative producers. Every member has a single producer token drawn from a five-value set.
coordinatorNote: The coverage half of my v6 finding is properly discharged, and I checked it from the obligation side rather than the map side so the completeness claim is independent of the artifact's own accounting. The single SHOULD-FIX is narrow but sits exactly where this lineage has been working: the map's discipline sentence promises one expected outcome per key, and the eleven new archive members break that promise eight times with an undefined disjunction that did not exist anywhere in v6. Nothing fails open, because both arms refuse. The reason I do not wave it through is that the contract already determines the answer in all eight cases — six map to a named admissionCheck and two to the profile-capacity codes it says it owns — so the disjunction buys nothing and costs the discrimination that member-level keying exists to provide. I also record that Codex v6 was still in flight and off my permission list, so this verdict scores the v6 round on my finding alone; v7 books that same exposure correctly in notFoldedThisSuccessor. DR-120 remains OPEN, no packager or toolchain is chosen, and nothing here marks DR-120 or DR-103 SATISFIED or authorizes docs/v2/implementation/.
